title: Hardware keystore Terraform bridge to Vault and SecretsManager
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Build a reusable Terraform module and companion operator that provisions and maintains a hardware-backed keystore bridge for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must support multiple key backends (cloud KMS providers + on-prem HSMs), maintain canonical secret sync to both Vault and AWS SecretsManager (customers may use either or both), and expose healthchecks and lightweight remediation hooks for the Redwood control plane.

Scope: module API, provider compatibility shim (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault + PKCS#11 HSMs), secret sync strategy (one-way canonical write from keystore to Secrets Stores + optional dual-write for migrations), automated rotation helpers, drift detection, and runtime health endpoints. The deliverable includes Terraform module, example stacks, CI tests for plan/apply drift detection, and an operator-runbook for incidents.

Non-functional requirements: idempotent changes, safe apply patterns for live key material, zero-downtime key provider rollover path, configurable retry/backoff for HSM network failures, and SLO for healthcheck reporting (<=30s test-to-fail detection).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module follows Redwood naming and inputs; supports providers: aws, gcp, azure, and pkcs11 (HSM).
Module can provision key resources and create wrapper objects that surface to Vault (via transit) and AWS SecretsManager with correct IAM roles/policies delegated.

A secrets-sync job (Terraform + small operator) reliably reconciles secret state from canonical keystore to Vault/SecretsManager and emits structured health metrics to Prometheus (endpoint + Grafana dashboard).
Healthchecks detect HSM unreachability, slow KMS RPCs, and sync backlog; documented automated remediation steps exist in runbook.
Module includes automated plan/apply CI with mocked provider tests and integ tests against a lightweight PKCS#11 emulator and AWS/GCP test accounts.
